purpose: An expert in this subdomain reasons about which VoIP channel model to operate (agent, wholesale reseller, or white-label, with who bills, who owns the customer, and who carries the risk under each), which small-business verticals to target on the strength of their phone-system pain, how to package hardware, setup, installation, monthly per-seat service, and support into one honestly priced offer with a defensible floor, and how to position that offer against incumbents and national brands without an unsubstantiated claim.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator is a local one-person or small-crew shop selling business phone systems to small firms such as dental practices, trucking outfits, restaurants, motels, and professional offices

all specific commission percentages, wholesale rates, retail prices, and tax figures live in the operator's current upstream agreements and jurisdiction rules; this KB describes only the mechanisms that generate them and how to verify each per deal
content is educational and operational knowledge for running the business, not personalized legal, tax, financial, or insurance advice
this KB covers the pre-sale economics and targeting stage; a signed, scoped deal is handed onward to the deployment discipline and a written support promise to the recurring-service discipline
exclusions: needs assessment, seat and feature mapping, phone versus softphone device selection, number-porting execution, network readiness, QoS, failover, E911 configuration work, cutover planning, and training - the sibling deployment KB owns these; this KB only raises the E911 flag and the number-ownership question at the sales stage

support ticket operations, escalation to the carrier or platform, churn signals and prevention, seat and feature expansion, SLA hygiene, renewals, and periodic account reviews - the sibling recurring-service KB owns these; this KB only defines what support the offer promises

stating any specific commission percentage, wholesale or retail price, tax rate, uptime figure, or market size as fact - channel economics appear only as mechanisms and qualitative bands to be verified against live agreements

asserting the operator's USF-class contribution, telecom-tax, or regulatory registration position - obligations are named by class and routed to a qualified telecom attorney or tax professional in the operator's jurisdiction
guaranteed-uptime or savings claims lacking a verified basis such as the upstream provider's published SLA or the customer's documented current bill
consumer and residential VoIP, carrier-scale interconnection engineering, and building an in-house softswitch platform

competency_questions.question: What separates the agent, wholesale reseller, and white-label ways of selling VoIP, and under each one who sends the bill, who owns the customer relationship, and who carries the credit and compliance risk?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CHANNEL_MODEL_TRIAD answers the three ownership questions (bill, customer, risk) distinctly for all three models and names what each answer implies for support burden and exit value

competency_questions.question: How does money actually reach an agent - what commission structures exist as mechanisms, what claws them back, and why is an agent book the weakest to sell?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AGENT_MODEL_MECHANICS describes upfront and residual commission mechanics, evergreen versus term-limited residual clauses, clawback triggers, and the exit-value weakness, with every figure deferred to the live partner agreement

competency_questions.question: What do I take on when I bill under my own brand as a wholesale reseller or white-label operator, and how do the two differ in margin capture and platform dependency?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESELLER_MODEL_MECHANICS and WHITELABEL_MODEL_MECHANICS each state the margin mechanism, the risks assumed (billing, collections, support, regulatory posture, platform lock-in), and how the two models differ

competency_questions.question: How do I choose which channel model to operate given my capital, support capacity, compliance appetite, and exit goals, and when is running a hybrid legitimate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MODEL_SELECTION_DECISION gives a criteria-scored decision procedure, names the hybrid pattern, and explains why the choice is expensive to reverse mid-book

competency_questions.question: Which regulatory and tax obligation classes shift onto me as I move from agent toward reseller, and who verifies my actual position before I invoice anyone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REGULATORY_EXPOSURE_BY_MODEL names the obligation classes (USF-class contributions, telecom tax collection, regulatory registration, 911-fee remittance), states that they attach differently by model, and routes verification to a qualified professional rather than asserting a position

competency_questions.question: What must every quote and scope say about E911 duties at the sales stage, and what may never be value-engineered out to win on price?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: E911_SALES_STAGE_FLAG states that Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class duties are flagged on every deployment quote, that current requirements are verified rather than assumed, and that no configuration is sold which would need to skip them

competency_questions.question: How do I pick which vertical niches to pursue and rank them into one or two beachheads instead of chasing every business with a phone?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NICHE_SELECTION_METHOD gives the pain-density and reachability criteria for profiling a vertical and SEGMENT_PRIORITIZATION_SCORECARD turns the profiles into a weighted ranking with a stated beachhead pick

competency_questions.question: What phone-system pain does a dental practice have, who actually decides there, and what must I never claim about compliance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DENTAL_SEGMENT_PROFILE names the missed-call-equals-missed-appointment pain, the office-manager gatekeeper and owner-dentist signer, the selling features, and the rule against asserting HIPAA compliance without platform and professional verification

competency_questions.question: What makes a trucking operation's seat mix different from a desk-bound office, and what is the crown jewel I must never endanger in the sale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TRUCKING_SEGMENT_PROFILE describes the dispatch-desk-plus-mobile-driver seat shape, the softphone-heavy mix, and the published dispatch number as the crown jewel whose porting risk is flagged to the deployment discipline

competency_questions.question: How do restaurants and motels differ as targets in call pattern, deal shape, credit risk, and E911 acuteness?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESTAURANT_SEGMENT_PROFILE covers peak-burst calls, small cheap seat counts, and business-failure credit risk; MOTEL_SEGMENT_PROFILE covers the room-extension deal shape, the legacy PBX retirement decision, and the acute room-level E911 duties

competency_questions.question: Why are small professional offices the retention backbone of a VoIP book, and how do I win them against national self-serve brands?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OFFICE_SEGMENT_PROFILE names the stable-seat low-support economics and referral density, and HONEST_COMPETITIVE_POSITIONING supplies the local-accountability counter to national self-serve competitors

competency_questions.question: How do I package hardware, setup, installation, monthly service, and support into one offer, and how is the per-seat price constructed with a floor I will not sign below?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OFFER_BUNDLE_ARCHITECTURE states what is bundled versus one-time and the purchase-versus-rental hardware decision, PER_SEAT_PRICING_MECHANICS constructs the seat price as wholesale cost plus support load plus pass-through handling plus margin with a documented floor, and SETUP_INSTALL_REVENUE assigns one-time revenue its cost-covering role

competency_questions.question: What support does the monthly price actually promise, and how does that promise bind both the seat price and the recurring-service operation downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SUPPORT_COMMITMENT_SCOPE defines included versus billable work classes and response expectations, and states that a heavier promise raises the seat floor and becomes the contract the recurring-service discipline must operate

competency_questions.question: What claims may I make when positioning against copper incumbents and national brands, what substantiation does each require, and what packet must be complete before a deal passes to deployment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIMS_SUBSTANTIATION_RULE binds savings claims to a documented bill audit and uptime language to the upstream published SLA, HONEST_COMPETITIVE_POSITIONING maps each rival to a truthful counter, and DEPLOYMENT_HANDOFF_GATE lists the definition-of-done checklist

glossary.definition: A channel arrangement where the carrier or platform bills the end customer, owns the account and the compliance posture, and pays the local operator a commission on billed revenue; the operator sells and advises but never invoices the customer for service.

A channel arrangement where the operator buys seats, trunks, and numbers at wholesale from an upstream provider, sets its own retail price, bills the end customer under its own brand, and therefore owns billing, collections, tier-1 support, and potentially a regulated-provider posture.

A hosted VoIP stack sold under the local operator's brand while a platform vendor runs the switching, portal, and usually the carrier relationships; it delivers reseller-style ownership of the customer without building infrastructure, at the price of deep dependency on one vendor.
The billable unit of monthly VoIP service, normally one user or extension with a feature pack; seat count times per-seat price is the backbone of the account's monthly recurring revenue.

The compounding monthly service revenue across all active seats and accounts; the asset this whole business exists to build, and the number an acquirer of the book will value ahead of any one-time revenue.

A commission clause paying the agent a share of billed revenue for as long as the referred customer stays active, as opposed to a term-limited residual that expires after a contract period; which clause governs is read from the partner agreement, never assumed.

The family of regulatory contribution and remittance duties (universal service style funds, telecom-specific taxes and fees, 911-fee remittances, registration duties) that can attach to whoever is treated as the service provider; which entity carries them varies by channel model and jurisdiction and must be verified by a qualified professional.

glossary.term: Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class duties
glossary.definition: The class of E911 rules for multi-line phone systems requiring direct 911 dialing without a prefix, on-site notification when 911 is dialed, and a dispatchable location conveyed with the call; current requirements are verified on every deployment and never skipped for price.

Reading the prospect's actual current phone bill line by line to establish what they pay today; the only honest basis for any savings comparison and a reliable source of discoveries such as unused lines and legacy surcharges.

The per-seat monthly amount below which a deal is refused because it no longer covers wholesale cost, allocated support load, and pass-through handling with margin left; the floor is computed from the operator's own current costs, not from a competitor's quote.

nodes.definition: Fix what this business actually is before any channel or niche decision: a local operator who sells and configures business phone systems for small firms, arranges the port of their existing numbers, and bills monthly per-seat service with support attached. The revenue stack has four layers - hardware margin and setup fees at signing, installation labor, monthly per-seat service that compounds into MRR, and ongoing support either bundled or billable - and this subdomain governs the choices that shape the stack: which channel model to operate under, which vertical segments to pursue, how to package the four layers into one offer, and how to position it truthfully. The output of the stage is a signed, scoped, honestly priced deal handed to the deployment discipline and a written support promise handed to the recurring-service discipline.

included: the stage boundary between selling economics and delivering service
the artifacts this stage must hand onward
excluded: deployment execution such as porting and cutover
recurring support operations and renewals

pros.claim: Naming the four revenue layers up front stops the operator from selling phones like a hardware dealer and starving the MRR asset
pros.example: an operator who frames the business around monthly seats declines a hardware-only sale that would have produced no recurring revenue and no support relationship

cons.claim: A rigid frame can blind the operator to legitimate adjacent revenue that does not fit the four layers
cons.example: refusing a paid one-off phone-bill audit for a non-customer because it is not seat revenue, when it is exactly how motels become customers

failure_modes: treating the business as installation work with a billing afterthought, so every month starts at zero
letting the sales stage promise deployment or support details the downstream disciplines never agreed to carry
acceptance_tests: the frame states all four revenue layers, the stage boundary, and the two handoff artifacts (scoped deal, written support promise)
revisit_triggers: the operator adds a structurally new revenue layer such as connectivity resale
the sibling disciplines renegotiate what the sales stage must hand them

base.update_signal: the business adds or drops a revenue layer or the handoff contract with the sibling disciplines changes

nodes.definition: Lay the three ways of selling VoIP side by side before committing to any of them, using three ownership questions that decide everything downstream. Who sends the bill: the carrier under the agent model, the operator under wholesale resale, the operator (on a vendor's platform) under white-label. Who owns the customer relationship: the carrier owns the account an agent referred; the reseller and white-label operator own their customers, which is what makes their book saleable. Who carries the risk: the agent carries almost none beyond commission clawback; the reseller carries credit risk, support burden, and a possible regulated-provider posture; the white-label operator carries those plus concentrated dependency on one platform vendor. The triad is a map, not a verdict - the verdict belongs to the model-selection decision.

included: the bill / customer / risk ownership map for all three models
what each ownership answer implies for support burden and exit value
excluded: the numeric economics of any one model
the choice among the models

pros.claim: Reducing the models to three ownership questions makes an otherwise fog-bound vendor landscape decidable by a small operator
pros.example: an operator who cannot articulate who bills the customer under a proposed partner program discovers, by asking, that the shiny program is plain agency with marketing paint

cons.claim: Real partner programs blur the triad with hybrid terms the clean map does not show
cons.example: a co-branded billing arrangement where the carrier invoices but the operator handles collections calls sits between agent and reseller and needs contract reading, not the map

failure_modes: signing a partner agreement without answering the three ownership questions in writing
assuming customer ownership follows from doing the selling, when the agreement gives the account to the carrier
acceptance_tests: for each of the three models the answers to who bills, who owns the customer, and who carries the risk are stated and mutually distinct
revisit_triggers: an upstream partner restructures its program terms across the triad
a hybrid arrangement appears that the three-way map cannot classify

base.update_signal: a partner agreement or program restructuring changes who bills, who owns the customer, or who carries the risk

nodes.definition: Describe how money reaches an agent as mechanisms with every figure deferred to the live partner agreement: an upfront payment class (a spiff or multiple of the first month's billing paid at activation) and a residual class (a percentage of the customer's billed monthly revenue for as long as the clause runs). The clauses that matter more than the headline rate: evergreen versus term-limited residuals, clawback triggers when a referred customer cancels or downgrades early, whether the residual survives the customer renegotiating directly with the carrier, and assignability - whether the commission stream can be sold. The structural weakness is that the book belongs to the carrier: an agent business sells for less because the buyer acquires a revenue stream contingent on someone else's contract, not customers.

included: why an agent book is weak to sell
excluded: any specific commission percentage stated as fact
wholesale margin mechanics

pros.claim: Agency lets an undercapitalized operator earn from day one with no billing system, no credit risk, and no regulatory posture
pros.example: a solo installer closes a ten-seat dental office as an agent and is paid by the carrier while owning nothing but the relationship and the install work

cons.claim: The agent surrenders pricing power, support control, and the account itself, and a clause change can reprice years of work
cons.example: a carrier unilaterally amends its schedule to end evergreen residuals for new orders and the agent's compounding income quietly becomes a term annuity

failure_modes: selling on the headline commission rate without reading clawback, evergreen, and assignability clauses
building years of pipeline on one carrier's program with no diversification
acceptance_tests: the mechanics distinguish upfront from residual classes and name the four clauses (evergreen, clawback, direct-renegotiation survival, assignability) as items to verify in the current agreement
revisit_triggers: the carrier amends its commission schedule or program terms
a clawback larger than expected lands and reveals a misread clause

base.update_signal: the operator's partner agreement is amended or a comparison of two live agreements shows a materially different clause structure

nodes.definition: Describe what billing under your own brand actually buys and costs. The margin mechanism: buy seats, trunks, and numbers at wholesale from an upstream provider, set retail, and keep the spread after subtracting allocated support cost and the handling of regulatory and tax pass-throughs - read the current wholesale rate card for the cost side, never this KB. What is assumed in exchange: invoicing and collections (including customers who do not pay), tier-1 support because your name is on the bill, the platform and carrier relationships, and possibly the posture of a regulated service provider with USF-class and telecom-tax consequences that a professional must assess. What is gained: pricing power, bundling freedom, the whole customer relationship, and an enterprise-valued book, because a buyer acquires transferable customer contracts rather than a commission stream.

included: the assumed risks: collections, tier-1 support, regulatory posture
why a reseller book carries enterprise value
excluded: specific wholesale or retail prices
the white-label variant
running the support operation itself

pros.claim: Owning the bill converts every installed seat into transferable enterprise value instead of a contingent commission
pros.example: at exit, a book of motel and office customers on the operator's own paper is valued on its MRR, while the equivalent agent residuals are discounted for carrier dependence

cons.claim: The operator inherits every 2am outage call and every unpaid invoice on day one of the model
cons.example: a restaurant customer folds owing three months of service and the reseller, not a carrier, absorbs the write-off and the disconnection awkwardness

failure_modes: adopting the model for margin before pricing in the support hours and collections effort it drags with it
invoicing customers before a professional has assessed the regulatory and tax posture of being the provider of record
acceptance_tests: the margin mechanism is stated as retail minus wholesale minus allocated support minus pass-through handling, with the wholesale side sourced from the live rate card, and all four assumed risks are named
revisit_triggers: the upstream provider changes wholesale rates or contract minimums
collections losses or support load exceed what the margin was built to absorb

base.update_signal: the wholesale rate card, contract minimums, or the professional assessment of provider-of-record posture changes

nodes.definition: Describe the middle path: the operator's brand on a platform vendor's stack. The vendor runs the switching, the portal, usually the upstream carrier relationships, and often the taxation engine; the operator gets reseller-style customer ownership and margin without building or operating infrastructure. The costs are concentration and lock-in: one vendor's price increase reprices the whole book, one vendor's stagnating feature set becomes the operator's competitive ceiling, one vendor's acquisition or failure is an existential event, and migrating away means re-porting numbers and re-provisioning every customer - so vendor selection and the exit terms in the platform agreement are the real decisions. A disclosure duty rides along: the brand may be yours, but when a customer or contract asks who operates the service, the answer must be truthful.

included: exit terms as a selection criterion
excluded: building an in-house softswitch
the disclosure scripting itself, which the claims rule owns

pros.claim: White-label delivers customer ownership and bundling freedom at a fraction of the operational surface of full resale
pros.example: a two-person shop brands the portal, sets its own seat prices, and ships quotes in week one while the vendor handles switching and the tax engine

cons.claim: Everything hangs on one vendor, and the lock-in is real because leaving means migrating every customer
cons.example: a platform vendor is acquired and sunsets the white-label program; the operator faces re-porting hundreds of numbers under deadline or losing the brand relationship

failure_modes: choosing the vendor on demo polish without reading exit, data-export, and number-release terms
letting the white-label brand imply the operator built and runs the network
acceptance_tests: the mechanism, the three concentration risks (repricing, feature ceiling, vendor failure), and exit terms as a first-class selection criterion are all stated
revisit_triggers: the platform vendor changes pricing, ownership, or program terms
a competing platform's exit terms or feature velocity materially improve

base.update_signal: platform vendor terms, ownership, or the operator's dependence on a single vendor changes materially

nodes.definition: Enumerate the obligation classes whose owner shifts with the channel model, and route the actual determination to a professional. The classes: USF-style contribution obligations, telecom-specific taxes and fees collected on customer invoices, regulatory registrations that can attach to a provider of record, and 911-fee remittances. Under agency these generally remain with the carrier that bills the customer; under wholesale resale the operator may become the regulated provider whose invoices must collect and remit them; white-label arrangements vary with how the vendor structures carrier-of-record status and its tax engine. This node's discipline is to keep a written exposure flag list per model, to refuse to invoice a single customer before a qualified telecom attorney or tax professional has assessed the operator's position in its jurisdiction, and never to state a rate, threshold, or exemption as fact from memory.

included: the obligation classes and how their ownership shifts by model
excluded: asserting any actual regulatory or tax position, rate, or exemption
E911 duties, which have their own flag node

pros.claim: Flagging obligation classes before choosing a model prevents the worst version of the mistake: discovering provider-of-record duties after a year of invoicing
pros.example: an operator weighing the jump from agent to reseller gets a professional read first and learns the compliance overhead changes the margin math before any customer is re-papered

cons.claim: Professional verification costs money and time up front, which tempts a small operator to skip it while small
cons.example: a shop with only a few seats defers the assessment, then the book grows and the accumulated uncorrected posture is far costlier to unwind

failure_modes: treating a platform vendor's marketing statement that it handles all taxes as a legal determination of the operator's own posture
copying another reseller's invoice format and assuming the same obligations apply in a different jurisdiction
acceptance_tests: a written exposure flag list exists per candidate model naming each obligation class, and no invoice is issued under a model whose posture a qualified professional has not assessed
no rate, threshold, or exemption is asserted in any customer-facing or internal pricing document without a professional source
revisit_triggers: the operator changes channel model or enters a new jurisdiction
an upstream vendor changes carrier-of-record structure or its tax-engine scope
a regulatory change in the USF-class family is announced

base.update_signal: a professional assessment is delivered, a jurisdiction or model changes, or a USF-class rule change is announced

nodes.definition: Hold the E911 line at the stage where deals are shaped, because a quote that ignores it poisons everything downstream. The Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class of duties for multi-line phone systems - direct 911 dialing with no prefix, on-site notification when 911 is dialed, and dispatchable location conveyed with the call - attaches to the deployments this business sells. At the sales stage the discipline is threefold: every quote and scope document carries an E911 scoping line so the cost of compliance is in the price from the first draft; current requirements are verified per deployment rather than recalled from memory, since the rule class evolves; and no configuration is ever proposed that would need to skip these duties to hit a price, with room-phone properties like motels flagged as the acute case. How the duties are actually configured is the deployment discipline's work - this node guarantees no deal reaches it unflagged.

included: the E911 scoping line on every quote
the refusal to sell a non-compliant configuration
excluded: E911 configuration, testing, and location provisioning work, which the deployment KB owns

pros.claim: Pricing E911 scoping into every first draft removes the temptation to strip it under negotiation pressure
pros.example: when a motel owner asks what can be cut to lower the quote, the operator can cut phone models or training hours but points to the E911 line as non-removable by rule, not by preference

cons.claim: A visible compliance line can lengthen small-deal conversations and occasionally lose a price-only buyer
cons.example: a four-seat restaurant buyer walks to a competitor who quoted lower by never mentioning E911, a deal this discipline accepts losing

failure_modes: quoting from a stale memory of the rules instead of verifying current requirements for the deployment type
letting a discount negotiation quietly drop the E911 scoping line to close the month
acceptance_tests: every outbound quote and scope document contains an E911 scoping line and a note that current requirements were verified for this deployment type
no proposal in the pipeline describes a configuration that would require skipping direct-dial, notification, or dispatchable-location duties
revisit_triggers: a change in the E911 rule class or its enforcement guidance is announced
a deployment type appears (shared tenant floors, campus-style motel blocks) whose treatment under the current rules is unclear

base.update_signal: the E911 rule class changes, enforcement guidance shifts, or a quote is found in the pipeline without the scoping line

nodes.definition: Turn the triad map and the per-model mechanics into one accountable choice, scored against four operator realities: capital (can you float hardware, receivables, and a billing stack), support capacity (who answers when a dental office's phones die at 8am), compliance appetite (is professional verification of a provider-of-record posture budgeted), and exit ambition (is the goal lifestyle income or a saleable MRR book). The decision procedure scores each model against these criteria in writing, admits the common hybrid - white-label or resale for the core vertical book, agency for out-of-footprint or oversized deals that would strain support - and records the losing options and why, because the choice is expensive to reverse: switching models mid-book means re-papering customers, re-training their billing expectations, and sometimes re-porting numbers.

included: recording the decision and its losers
excluded: the underlying model mechanics
offer packaging, which consumes this decision

pros.claim: A written, criteria-scored choice prevents the default drift into whichever model the loudest vendor rep was selling
pros.example: scored against support capacity, a solo operator discovers full resale loses to white-label despite better margin, because the 2am call has no one to roll to

cons.claim: Scoring can rationalize a preference already made, especially when exit ambition is aspirational rather than honest
cons.example: an operator who wants the reseller identity scores compliance appetite generously, then skips the professional assessment the score assumed

failure_modes: choosing resale margin while resourcing support like an agent
running a hybrid without rules for which deals go to which model, so the choice is remade ad hoc on every quote
acceptance_tests: a written decision memo scores all candidate models on capital, support capacity, compliance appetite, and exit ambition, names the chosen model and hybrid rules, and carries the regulatory and E911 flags forward
revisit_triggers: realized support burden or collections losses contradict the scoring assumptions
an upstream program change repricess the chosen model
the operator's capital or exit ambitions change materially

base.update_signal: operating evidence (support hours, collections, program changes) contradicts a scored assumption in the decision memo

nodes.definition: Screen candidate verticals with criteria that predict repeatable, referenceable business instead of chasing every firm with a phone. The criteria: phone-pain density (does a missed call directly cost the business revenue, as it does when an appointment, a load, or a takeout order rides on it), decision-maker reachability (can the person who signs be reached without a procurement layer), referral clustering (do owners in the vertical talk to each other at association meetings so one good install seeds the next), seat shape (how many seats, how stable, desk or mobile), and install repeatability (does the tenth deployment look like the third, so templates compound). The method produces a written pain profile per candidate vertical - the five profiled here are dental, trucking, restaurant, motel, and professional office - which the scorecard then ranks.

excluded: the ranking itself, which the scorecard owns
any one vertical's detailed profile

pros.claim: Screening on pain density and referral clustering concentrates marketing into rooms where one happy customer recruits the next
pros.example: after one dental install, the office manager mentions it at a local study club and two practices call in the same quarter - a dynamic generic small-office marketing never produces

cons.claim: Hard screening can discard viable opportunistic deals that arrive from outside the chosen verticals
cons.example: a veterinary clinic - functionally a dental office with different signage - is turned away because it is not on the list, when the install template fits almost unchanged

failure_modes: picking verticals by personal familiarity instead of the criteria, then discovering the segment has no referral fabric
writing profiles from imagination instead of ride-alongs, bill audits, and conversations with real front desks
acceptance_tests: each candidate vertical has a written profile scoring all five criteria with at least one observed example per criterion, not assumptions
revisit_triggers: an unprofiled vertical produces repeated inbound demand
a profiled vertical's pain changes because its tooling changes (for example online ordering absorbing restaurant call volume)

base.update_signal: observed win rates or referral behavior in a vertical contradict its profiled criteria scores

nodes.definition: Profile the dental practice, where the front desk is a revenue organ: every unanswered ring during lunch or hygiene-recall season is a missed appointment or an emergency patient dialing the practice down the street. The recurring pain: a single line that goes busy, no after-hours routing for dental emergencies, no overflow when the scheduler is with a patient, and voicemail nobody checks until Monday. The selling features map straight onto it: auto-attendant with an emergency branch, hunt from front desk to back office, after-hours routing to the on-call dentist's cell, and voicemail-to-email so the morning recall list is complete. The buying structure is a gatekeeper-signer pair: the office manager evaluates and can veto, the owner-dentist signs; sell the demo to the office manager. One discipline is non-negotiable: never claim the phone system is HIPAA compliant - questions about recorded calls, voicemail transcripts, or business-associate agreements are routed to the platform vendor and a qualified advisor for verification. Seats are stable, hours are civilized, and the support load is daytime-only, which is why this segment anchors many local books.

included: front-desk pain and its feature map
excluded: asserting HIPAA compliance
clinical or practice-management software integration work

pros.claim: Dental practices combine acute measurable phone pain with stable seats and a dense referral fabric of study clubs and suppliers
pros.example: one practice install with an emergency auto-attendant branch becomes the reference that closes two more practices in the same professional circle

cons.claim: The compliance-adjacent questions demand careful handling a phone generalist can fumble into a lost deal or a false claim
cons.example: asked point-blank whether voicemail transcription is HIPAA compliant, an unprepared seller either overclaims (a liability) or stalls visibly (a lost demo)

failure_modes: pitching the owner-dentist and treating the office manager as an obstacle instead of the real evaluator
asserting compliance status to close, creating liability the operator cannot cover
acceptance_tests: the profile names the pain, the feature map, the gatekeeper-signer pair, and the routed-not-asserted handling of HIPAA-class questions
revisit_triggers: practice-management platforms absorb call handling and shift where the pain lives
a platform vendor changes what compliance-supporting terms it will sign

base.update_signal: observed dental win-loss patterns or compliance-question handling outcomes contradict the profile

nodes.definition: Profile the trucking and dispatch operation, whose phone system is a revenue dispatch tool rather than a desk amenity. The shape: a small office core (dispatch, billing, safety) and a large mobile fringe of drivers who must be reachable through the company's published number, not their personal cells. The pain: dispatch lines congested while brokers are calling loads to whoever answers first, missed broker calls that cost real freight, and drivers unreachable when a receiver needs a delivery window. The fit: softphone-heavy seat mixes on drivers' phones, ring groups that hunt dispatch then overflow to mobiles, find-me-follow-me for owner-operators, and text-enabled main numbers where the platform supports them. The crown jewel is the published dispatch number that brokers and shippers have saved for years - its continuity is existential, so the porting risk flag goes on the deal from the first conversation and the mechanics belong to the deployment discipline. Seat revenue skews toward many low-cost mobile extensions rather than premium desk phones, so hardware margin is thin and the money is in the recurring mix.

excluded: porting execution
fleet telematics and ELD systems, which are not phone service

pros.claim: Trucking outfits are underserved by desk-phone-oriented competitors, so a softphone-literate local operator differentiates immediately
pros.example: a quote built around driver softphones and a dispatch ring group wins against a national quote that priced a desk phone for every driver who is never at a desk

cons.claim: Mobile-first fleets generate diffuse support questions on personal devices the operator does not control
cons.example: a driver's personal phone update breaks the softphone app on a Sunday and the support call lands on the operator though nothing in the sold system changed

failure_modes: quoting hardware-heavy configurations that misread where trucking value lives
promising a cutover date before the published dispatch number's portability has been flagged and checked
acceptance_tests: the profile states the office-core-plus-mobile-fringe shape, the softphone-forward fit, and the dispatch-number continuity flag carried on every trucking deal
revisit_triggers: dispatch moves into load-board and TMS platforms and shifts the pain away from voice
support data shows mobile-device issues dominating trucking tickets

base.update_signal: trucking deal shapes or support ticket mixes contradict the profiled seat shape

nodes.definition: Profile the restaurant, whose call pattern is a twice-daily burst: the lunch and dinner rushes when a busy signal is a lost takeout order walking to a competitor. The pain: one line ringing into a kitchen that cannot answer, no hold or overflow, and hours-and-location questions consuming the only person at the register. The fit is small and cheap: an auto-attendant that answers hours-location-menu questions without a human, a takeout queue with hold, overflow to a manager's mobile, and a seat count that rarely passes a handful. The segment's economics demand honesty with oneself: seat counts are low, the environment is greasy and loud for installs, support calls arrive at the worst possible hours (mid-rush), and restaurants fail at a high rate relative to other small businesses - so contract exposure, hardware recovery terms, and deposit-class protections belong in the deal shape, and the segment is better as volume filler than as the beachhead a book is built on.

included: peak-burst call pattern and its small feature fit
business-failure credit risk in the deal shape
excluded: online-ordering platforms and POS systems
collections execution, which the recurring-service discipline owns

pros.claim: The pain is vivid and demonstrable in one visit, which makes the sale concrete and fast
pros.example: standing at the counter at noon while the phone rings unanswered sells the auto-attendant better than any brochure

cons.claim: High business mortality converts signed contracts into write-offs and stranded hardware
cons.example: a restaurant folds eight months into a term; the operator recovers two scuffed phones and writes off the remaining contract value

failure_modes: building revenue projections on restaurant seats as if they had office-grade persistence
shaping restaurant deals with no hardware recovery or deposit-class terms
acceptance_tests: the profile states the burst pattern, the minimal feature fit, and the credit-risk-aware deal shape with recovery terms
revisit_triggers: online ordering absorbs enough call volume to change the pain profile
realized churn or write-off experience in the segment shifts its economics

base.update_signal: segment churn, write-off, or call-pattern evidence contradicts the profiled economics

nodes.definition: Profile the motel and small-hospitality property, whose deal shape is unlike every other segment: a few real seats at the front desk and office, plus dozens of low-use room extensions that exist for guest service and for safety. The pain: an aging analog PBX with failing line cards nobody can service, wake-up calls and front-desk transfers that must keep working, and an owner-operator buyer who expects equipment to last decades and prices accordingly. The design fork that shapes the economics: retire the old PBX in favor of ATA banks driving the existing analog room phones (cheap, preserves wiring) versus IP phones in every room (clean, costly) - the fork is decided in deployment, but the quote must price both paths honestly. E911 is at its most acute here: room-level dispatchable location and direct 911 dialing from every room phone are exactly what the Kari's Law / RAY BAUM class exists for, so the sales-stage flag is mandatory and a motel deal that resists E911 scoping is declined, not discounted. Sold well, motels yield large per-account installs, sticky service, and referrals through lodging associations.

included: acute E911 flagging and the walk-away rule
excluded: property-management-system integration execution
E911 provisioning work, which deployment owns

pros.claim: One motel deal carries the install revenue and extension count of many small-office deals, with sticky multi-year service
pros.example: a several-dozen-room property produces a hardware-and-labor install plus a recurring extension base no four-seat office can match

cons.claim: Room-phone deployments concentrate compliance duty and wiring surprises into one price-sensitive buyer's project
cons.example: mid-install, decades-old wiring to a room block proves dead and the fixed quote absorbs the re-run unless the contract priced discovery honestly

failure_modes: quoting room phones as if they were office seats and mispricing both hardware and support
discounting away the E911 scoping under owner pressure instead of declining the deal
acceptance_tests: every motel quote prices the ATA-versus-IP fork explicitly, carries the acute E911 flag with room-level location scoping, and documents the walk-away rule for E911 resistance
revisit_triggers: the E911 rule class or its guidance for hospitality properties changes
install experience shows the wiring-condition assumption in quotes is systematically wrong

base.update_signal: hospitality E911 guidance changes or motel install experience contradicts the quoted assumptions

nodes.definition: Profile the small professional office - law, accounting, insurance, realty - the retention backbone of a local VoIP book. The pain is quieter than the other segments but chronic: a receptionist juggling lines with no hunt group, missed client calls during meetings, no voicemail-to-email so messages die in a blinking light, and conference calling that embarrasses the firm. The fit: reception hunt groups, direct-dial numbers per professional, voicemail-to-email, and simple conferencing. Seats are the most stable in the book (firms rarely shrink or move), support load is low and business-hours, and the referral fabric is dense - the accountant knows the lawyer knows the insurance broker. The catch is competition: every national self-serve brand targets this segment with slick signup flows, so the win depends on positioning local install, one accountable human, and vertical fluency rather than price. This is usually the correct first beachhead: not the most vivid pain, but the best lifetime economics per hour of support.

excluded: document management or practice software integration
the positioning playbook itself

pros.claim: Office seats combine the longest retention and lowest support cost in the book, compounding MRR quietly
pros.example: a five-seat accounting firm installed once generates years of untouched recurring revenue and two referrals from its professional circle

cons.claim: The segment is the most contested, and a price-only pitch loses to national self-serve every time
cons.example: a law office comparing quotes sees a national brand's per-seat price below the local floor and chooses it unless local accountability was sold first

failure_modes: competing on per-seat price against national scale instead of on install and accountability
underestimating the segment because its pain is undramatic, and skipping it for flashier verticals
acceptance_tests: the profile states the reception pain map, the stability-and-support economics, and the local-accountability basis for winning against self-serve
revisit_triggers: national brands add local-install partner programs that erode the differentiation
observed office retention or support load contradicts the profiled economics

base.update_signal: office-segment retention, support, or competitive-loss data contradicts the profile

nodes.definition: Convert the five vertical profiles into one or two beachhead picks with a weighted scorecard instead of enthusiasm. The criteria, weighted by the operator's situation: seat stability (office and dental high, restaurant low), per-account seat and extension count (motel high, restaurant low), support burden and its hours (dental civilized, restaurant mid-rush, trucking diffuse), sales-cycle length and decision-maker access (owner-operators fast, anything with partners slower), referral density inside the vertical, and credit risk from business mortality. Each profiled segment is scored per criterion with the evidence from its profile, the weights are declared before scoring to prevent retrofitting, and the output is a ranked list with one or two beachheads and an explicit parking decision for the rest. The scorecard is kept, because it is re-run on evidence: win rates, realized support hours, churn, and referral behavior all feed back into the scores.

included: the weighted criteria and declared-weights discipline
the ranked output with beachhead and parked segments
excluded: the underlying vertical profiles
offer construction for the chosen beachhead

pros.claim: Declaring weights before scoring exposes the difference between a strategy and a rationalization
pros.example: an operator drawn to motels for the big installs sees, once support-burden weighting is applied honestly, that offices should anchor the first year with motels as the second wave

cons.claim: A scorecard built on profile estimates inherits their errors with false numerical authority
cons.example: referral density guessed rather than observed puts dental two ranks too high until the first quarter's actual referral count corrects it

failure_modes: scoring segments on imagined data and never re-running with observed results
picking three or four beachheads, which is the same as picking none
acceptance_tests: the scorecard shows declared weights, per-segment scores traceable to profile evidence, a one-or-two beachhead pick, and a written parking decision for the rest
revisit_triggers: a quarter of win-loss, support-hour, or churn evidence contradicts a segment's score
the operator's capacity changes enough to justify activating a parked segment

base.update_signal: observed win-loss, support, churn, or referral evidence changes a segment's score or the beachhead pick

nodes.definition: Assemble hardware, setup, installation, monthly service, and support into one named offer with a deliberate shape, instead of a parts list the prospect must assemble. The architectural decisions: which support tier is bundled into the monthly and which work is billable; whether hardware is bought outright (customer owns it, bigger day-one invoice) or amortized into the monthly as a rental (smoother cash, deeper lock-in, hardware recovery terms required); what is always one-time (installation labor, network prep); and what every bundle must carry regardless of shape - the E911 scoping line, which is never value-engineered out. The offer presents one accountable monthly price per seat plus one understood one-time cost, is standardized as a core bundle with pre-built vertical option packs (a dental emergency-routing pack, a motel room-extension pack) rather than bespoke per-deal engineering, and is honest about totals: whatever is amortized is disclosed with term and total cost.

included: core bundle plus vertical option packs
excluded: the per-seat price computation
delivery of installation or training

pros.claim: A single accountable offer shape closes faster and defends margin better than itemized quotes that invite line-by-line shopping
pros.example: a motel owner comparing an itemized competitor quote against one clear monthly-plus-install offer negotiates the competitor line by line and signs the bundle

cons.claim: Bundling hides cost detail some sophisticated buyers demand, and rental structures can be mistaken for hidden financing
cons.example: an accountant prospect asks what portion of the monthly is hardware amortization and walks when the seller cannot decompose the number on the spot

failure_modes: engineering a bespoke bundle per deal so no two customers are comparable and no template compounds
amortizing hardware into the monthly without disclosing term and total cost, which reads as deception at renewal
acceptance_tests: the offer sheet shows the core bundle, its vertical option packs, the purchase-versus-rental fork with disclosed totals, the one-time components, and the E911 scoping line present in every variant
revisit_triggers: win-loss evidence shows the bundle shape losing to itemized or differently shaped competitors
a new vertical option pack is needed for an activated segment
hardware supply or platform pricing changes the purchase-versus-rental balance

base.update_signal: win-loss patterns, segment activation, or upstream pricing shifts force a change in bundle shape or option packs

nodes.definition: Construct the per-seat monthly price as a mechanism whose every input is verified per deal, never quoted from folklore. The build-up: the wholesale seat cost read from the current upstream rate card; an allocation for the support minutes the tier promises (heavier promised scope raises the seat, which is why the support commitment is defined first); the handling of regulatory and tax pass-throughs as the professional assessment of the chosen model dictates, stated on the quote so the customer knows whether fees are included or itemized; and margin. From the build-up comes the floor: the seat price below which a deal is refused because it no longer carries its own costs - computed from the operator's own numbers, not from a competitor's quote. Tiering expresses feature packs (basic seat, front-desk seat, mobile-only extension) with the same mechanism per tier. This node never supplies figures; it supplies the arithmetic shape and the rule that each input is re-verified when its source (rate card, support data, professional guidance) changes.

included: the self-computed floor and refusal rule
excluded: any actual price or rate stated as fact
competitive discount tactics beyond the floor rule

pros.claim: A floor derived from the operator's own cost build-up makes discount pressure survivable and walk-aways calm
pros.example: against a competitor's below-cost quote, the operator declines to match, shows the buyer what the lower quote must be leaving out, and keeps the deals that value scope

cons.claim: Cost-up pricing ignores what the segment would happily pay, leaving value on the table in low-competition niches
cons.example: trucking deals close so fast at the floor-plus-standard-margin that the operator realizes a value-based tier was warranted for dispatch-critical seats

failure_modes: quoting seats from a stale rate card after the upstream repriced wholesale
signing below the floor to win a lighthouse logo and normalizing the exception into the book
acceptance_tests: a pricing sheet exists showing the four-input build-up per tier, the computed floor, the pass-through treatment as professionally advised, and the date each input was last verified
no signed deal in the book prices a seat below the documented floor without a written, dated exception rationale
revisit_triggers: the upstream rate card or contract minimums change
realized support minutes per seat drift from the allocation
the professional guidance on pass-through treatment is updated

base.update_signal: any pricing input source changes: the rate card, observed support minutes, or professional pass-through guidance

nodes.definition: Assign the one-time revenue layer its correct role: hardware margin, installation labor, network preparation, configuration, and initial training exist to cover the cost of acquiring and standing up the customer, so the monthly margin stays clean from month one - not to be a profit center whose padding kills winnable deals, and not to be given away so completely that every new customer starts as a loss the MRR must dig out of. The pricing discipline: labor priced from a realistic site-survey-informed estimate rather than optimism, hardware margin taken honestly at a level the customer could sanity-check against retail, and network prep (the switch, cabling fixes, a router the deployment discipline will insist on) scoped and charged rather than absorbed. Amortizing setup into the monthly is a legitimate cash-flow accommodation when the term and the total paid over it are disclosed - the same honesty rule as hardware rental. Which crews, methods, and hours the install actually takes is the deployment discipline's knowledge; this node prices its output.

included: the cost-covering role of one-time revenue
survey-informed labor and honest hardware margin
excluded: install execution and crew management
the monthly seat price construction

pros.claim: One-time revenue that covers acquisition cost lets the operator survive the early months of a growing book without starving
pros.example: a motel install priced to cover its labor and hardware means the account is profitable from its first monthly invoice instead of eighteen months in

cons.claim: Heavy upfront pricing repels exactly the cash-tight small buyers the verticals are full of
cons.example: a family restaurant declines a solid monthly offer because the day-one install invoice equals a month of revenue, when a disclosed amortized structure would have closed

failure_modes: waiving install fees under pressure until every new account opens underwater
padding one-time lines as the profit center and losing deals the recurring margin would have justified
acceptance_tests: each quote's one-time section traces to a site-survey-informed labor estimate and honest hardware margin, and any amortized structure shows term and total
revisit_triggers: realized install hours diverge from the estimates quotes are built on
hardware cost or availability changes the margin balance

base.update_signal: install-hour actuals, hardware costs, or close-rate evidence on upfront pricing change the balance

nodes.definition: Define at offer time exactly what support the monthly price buys, because this promise is simultaneously a pricing input, a contract term, and the workload the recurring-service discipline will have to live with. The scope decisions: response expectations stated in honest business terms (same-business-day callback, not fictitious guarantee language); which work classes are included in the monthly (fault diagnosis, carrier escalation, remote fixes) versus billable (moves-adds-changes beyond an included allowance, training refreshers, on-site visits not caused by the operator's own work); and where the operator's responsibility hands off to the platform or carrier escalation path. The model choice feeds directly in: an agent's support promise can only ever be best-effort liaison because the carrier owns the fix, while a reseller's promise is the product. The qualitative sizing law: every widening of included scope raises the seat floor, so scope creep in the offer sheet is a pricing decision whether or not anyone repriced.

excluded: running the support operation, tickets, and escalations, which the recurring-service KB owns
uptime guarantee language, which the claims rule governs

pros.claim: A written included-versus-billable boundary prevents the silent scope creep that turns support into unpaid labor
pros.example: when a dental office asks for a third staff-training session, the offer sheet's included allowance makes the billable answer a reference to paper instead of an awkward negotiation

cons.claim: A tightly lawyered scope can read as nickel-and-diming in segments where goodwill is the retention engine
cons.example: billing a motel owner for a ten-minute voicemail tweak wins the invoice and plants the churn seed the recurring discipline harvests later

failure_modes: promising reseller-grade support while operating under a model where the carrier owns the fix
leaving support scope implicit so every customer believes everything is included forever
acceptance_tests: the offer's support section lists included and billable work classes, honest response language, the escalation handoff, and is signed off as a pricing input to the seat floor
revisit_triggers: realized support minutes per seat exceed what the included scope was priced for
the recurring-service discipline reports the written scope diverging from what customers are actually given

base.update_signal: support-minute actuals or recurring-service feedback show the written scope and the operated reality diverging

nodes.definition: Bind everything customer-facing to a substantiation rule that is a gate, not a tone suggestion. Disclosure first: the operating model is stated truthfully in contracts and answered truthfully when asked - under agency the customer is told whose paper they will be on, under white-label the answer to who runs the network is honest even while the brand is yours. Claims need evidence in hand before they are made: a savings claim exists only after a bill audit of the customer's actual current bill, and is framed against that documented bill; uptime language never exceeds what the upstream provider's published SLA verifiably supports, and absolute guarantee words are refused entirely; feature claims are demonstrable in the demo environment. No fear-selling: no invented copper-retirement deadlines, no manufactured urgency, no exploiting a prospect's inability to evaluate the technology. Vulnerable-buyer care is explicit: with buyers showing limited English, limited tech familiarity, or advanced age, the pace slows, the disclosure goes plain-language and written, total costs are stated, and time to decide is offered - the deals this loses are deals that should be lost.

included: model disclosure in contract and conversation
evidence-before-claim for savings, uptime, and features
excluded: the competitive playbook itself
SLA operations and renewal conduct, which the recurring-service KB carries forward

pros.claim: Substantiated claims survive the customer's later scrutiny, which is where local reputations are actually made
pros.example: a motel owner rechecks the promised savings against the old bill a year in, finds the comparison honest, and becomes the reference the lodging association hears about

cons.claim: Refusing guarantee language and urgency tactics concedes deals to competitors who use both freely
cons.example: a prospect chooses the rival who promised total uptime in writing; the discipline holds and the rival's first outage becomes next year's win-back

failure_modes: quoting typical savings percentages from marketing folklore with no bill audit behind them
letting white-label branding drift into implying an owned network
closing a visibly confused buyer on the spot instead of slowing down
acceptance_tests: every claim in active sales materials maps to its evidence: savings to a bill audit, uptime to the upstream published SLA, features to the demo environment
contracts state the operating model truthfully, and the vulnerable-buyer practices are written into the sales process, not left to discretion
revisit_triggers: the upstream published SLA changes, invalidating uptime language in materials
a claim is challenged by a prospect, customer, or competitor
a sales conversation is flagged as having pressured a vulnerable buyer

base.update_signal: an SLA change, a challenged claim, or a flagged sales interaction shows the rule being outrun by practice

nodes.definition: Position the offer against the three rivals it actually meets, with a truthful counter for each. Against the incumbent's legacy copper and aging on-premise PBXs: sell the bill audit (unused lines and legacy surcharges surface by themselves), modern features the old system cannot do, and end-of-life service reality - never an invented retirement deadline or a savings figure with no audited bill behind it. Against national self-serve UCaaS brands: concede their price and polish, and sell what they structurally cannot deliver - a human who shows up, local install and network prep, one accountable throat to choke, and vertical fluency (the dental emergency branch, the motel room block) that a generic signup flow will never configure. Against other local MSPs and phone dealers: sell references in the chosen verticals and the coherence of the bundled offer rather than badmouthing. The governing rule inherits from the claims gate: every positioning sentence must survive the substantiation test, and a deal that can only be won by lying is lost on purpose.

included: the three rival classes and their truthful counters
the bill audit as the copper conversion tool
excluded: claim evidence rules, which the substantiation gate owns
price-floor arithmetic

pros.claim: Rival-specific counters keep the pitch on ground the local operator actually holds instead of fighting national scale on price
pros.example: against a national brand's lower seat price, the pitch shifts to who reruns the cable when the fax line dies mid-port, and the office signs locally

cons.claim: Honest positioning is slower than fear and discounts, and shows its value only over quarters
cons.example: a quarter of lost price-only deals precedes the first win-back from a rival's failed install, testing the operator's nerve

failure_modes: drifting into copper-retirement scare scripts because they close faster
matching a below-floor competitor price instead of repositioning scope, breaking the pricing discipline
acceptance_tests: a positioning document maps each rival class to its counter, every sentence passes the substantiation test, and win-loss notes record deals deliberately lost to the honesty rule
revisit_triggers: win-loss evidence shows a counter failing repeatedly in live deals
a rival class changes structurally, such as national brands adding local-install partners

base.update_signal: win-loss patterns or a structural change in a rival class invalidate a mapped counter

nodes.definition: Gate every deal out of the economics stage with a definition-of-done, because the deployment and recurring-service disciplines inherit whatever this stage leaves vague. The checklist a deal must pass: the channel model decision is documented with its regulatory flags routed to professional verification; the deal sits inside a scored beachhead segment or carries a written exception; the offer is priced at or above the documented floor with the E911 scoping line intact; hardware and any amortization structure are disclosed with term and total; the support promise is written in included-versus-billable form; every claim made in the sale maps to its substantiation; and the number-ownership question - who controls the numbers to be ported, on whose account do they sit, is there any porting-consent complication - is asked and its answer recorded, so the deployment discipline starts porting from facts rather than assumptions. Deals failing any line bounce back to the owning node rather than limping forward, and repeated bounce patterns are themselves a signal that an upstream node needs repair.

included: the bounce-back rule and bounce-pattern signal
excluded: executing the port, survey, or cutover
operating the support promise after handoff

pros.claim: A hard gate converts sales enthusiasm into deployable fact and protects the two downstream disciplines from inherited vagueness
pros.example: the gate catches a trucking deal where nobody recorded whose account the dispatch number sits on, a fact that would have surfaced as a mid-cutover port rejection

cons.claim: A strict gate adds friction and delay to small clean deals that need none of it
cons.example: a four-seat office deal identical to the last ten waits two days for checklist processing that changes nothing

failure_modes: waving deals through at month-end, which is exactly when the vaguest deals are signed
treating repeated bounces as clerical noise instead of evidence an upstream node is broken
acceptance_tests: every deal entering deployment carries the completed checklist with all seven lines answered, and bounced deals show the owning node and the repair made
revisit_triggers: the deployment or recurring-service discipline reports handoff packets missing information the checklist should have caught
bounce-pattern review shows one checklist line failing repeatedly

base.update_signal: downstream disciplines report gaps the checklist missed or bounce patterns concentrate on one line

edges.why_related: the ownership map is drawn for the business the frame defines: a local operator building an MRR book on the four-layer stack
vertical screening criteria only make sense against the frame's revenue stack and stage scope
the substantiation gate binds the customer-facing surface of the business the frame establishes
the E911 flag discipline attaches to every deployment the framed business sells
agent commission mechanics elaborate the carrier-bills, carrier-owns corner of the triad map
wholesale resale mechanics elaborate the operator-bills, operator-owns corner of the triad map
white-label mechanics elaborate the middle position of the triad where brand and platform ownership split
which entity carries USF-class and tax obligations follows from the triad's who-bills and who-owns answers
the selection decision scores agency using the commission, clawback, and exit-value mechanics
the selection decision scores resale using the margin mechanism and its four assumed risks
the selection decision scores white-label using the dependency and lock-in trade the mechanics expose
compliance appetite is one of the four scoring criteria and its content is the exposure flag list
the dental profile is the screening method applied to one candidate vertical
the trucking profile applies the same five screening criteria to the dispatch vertical
the restaurant profile applies the screening criteria and surfaces the segment's credit-risk caveat
the motel profile applies the screening criteria to the room-extension deal shape
the office profile applies the screening criteria to the stable-seat backbone segment
the scorecard consumes the dental profile's evidence as scores on the weighted criteria
the bundle can only be architected once the model decides who bills and what support can be promised
the beachhead pick determines which vertical option packs the core bundle needs first
the seat price is computed for the bundle shape: what is bundled, rented, or one-time
the support tier bundled into the monthly is an architectural decision the scope must make precise
every positioning counter must pass the substantiation gate before it is used in a live deal
the floor and its refusal rule are what positioning falls back on under discount pressure
the gate checks that the claims made to win the deal each map to their substantiation
quotes must state pass-through treatment as the professional assessment of the chosen model dictates, so pricing cannot finalize ahead of that guidance
edges.risk_of_conflict: invoices collect or omit regulatory fees on a posture nobody verified

edges.why_related: room-phone deals carry the acute direct-dial and dispatchable-location duties, so motel quotes are constrained to include room-level E911 scoping
edges.risk_of_conflict: a price-shaved motel quote ships without room-level location scoping

edges.why_related: every bundle variant must carry the E911 scoping line, which constrains what cost-cutting the architecture may offer
edges.risk_of_conflict: a stripped-down bundle variant quietly omits compliance scoping

edges.why_related: white-label branding is constrained by the disclosure duty: the brand may be the operator's, the answer about who runs the network may not be false
edges.risk_of_conflict: brand language drifts into implying an owned network

edges.why_related: loading profit into the one-time layer competes with carrying margin in the monthly seat, and each layer's pricing pressures the other
edges.resolution_rule: recurring durability wins: one-time revenue covers acquisition and install cost, margin lives in the monthly seat; amortize upfront cost into the monthly only for cash-constrained buyers, with term and total disclosed

edges.why_related: the white-label brand story pulls toward looking like a network owner while the disclosure rule pulls toward naming the platform reality
edges.resolution_rule: disclosure dominates: keep the brand on the portal and the invoice, but answer who-runs-the-network questions truthfully and put the platform relationship in the contract

edges.why_related: a single standardized bundle resists the per-vertical tailoring the segment evidence keeps requesting, and full tailoring destroys the template economics
edges.resolution_rule: one core bundle wins as the base; vertical differences are expressed only as pre-built option packs, and bespoke engineering is reserved for deals above a seat threshold the operator sets in writing

edges.why_related: the support minutes the tier promises are a direct cost input: widening included scope raises the computed seat floor
the chosen model determines who owns the fix, which causally bounds what support promise can honestly be written
the segment's business-mortality credit risk pushes deposit-class terms and hardware recovery provisions into the pricing of restaurant deals
positioning is drafted after the beachhead pick so the counters speak the chosen verticals' language
a deal is assembled as a bundle first and only then presented to the gate's checklist
gate bounce patterns and downstream deployment experience feed back into how segments are scored and picked
realized support burden under the written scope is the evidence that forces the model decision memo to be rescored
both are appointment-and-reception businesses with stable daytime seats, so their install templates and support expectations rhyme

conflict_axes.name: customer_ownership_vs_capital_and_burden
conflict_axes.description: Owning the bill and the customer (resale, white-label) builds a saleable MRR book but demands capital, collections, and support capacity; agency needs almost nothing but owns nothing.
poles: own the customer, the bill, and the risk
refer the customer and keep only a commission
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: score the models against honest capital, support, compliance, and exit answers; hybrids are legitimate when the routing rule is written down

conflict_axes.name: upfront_cash_vs_recurring_durability
conflict_axes.description: Padding hardware and install revenue feeds this quarter; keeping the monthly seat rich feeds the asset the business exists to build, and each pulls pricing toward itself.
poles: harvest one-time revenue now
protect monthly margin and MRR durability
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: one-time covers cost, monthly carries margin; amortization is a disclosed accommodation, not a hidden financing trick

conflict_axes.name: brand_story_vs_disclosure_duty
conflict_axes.description: White-label branding wants the operator to look like the network; the disclosure rule requires truthful answers about who actually runs it.
poles: present a seamless own-brand service
disclose the platform and carrier reality
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: brand the experience, disclose the structure: portal and invoice carry the operator's name, contract and honest answers carry the facts

conflict_axes.name: niche_focus_vs_opportunistic_breadth
conflict_axes.description: Beachhead discipline compounds references and templates inside one or two verticals, while real pipelines keep offering decent deals from outside them.
poles: stay inside the scored beachheads
take good deals wherever they appear
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: beachheads get proactive effort; off-list deals are taken only when they fit the existing bundle without new engineering, and are logged as scorecard evidence

conflict_axes.name: standard_bundle_vs_vertical_tailoring
conflict_axes.description: Template economics demand one repeatable offer; segment evidence demands dental emergency branches, motel room packs, and trucking softphone mixes.
poles: one standardized core bundle
per-vertical bespoke offers
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: core bundle plus pre-built vertical option packs; bespoke work only above a written seat threshold

conflict_axes.name: margin_floor_vs_winnable_price
conflict_axes.description: The computed floor protects the book's economics; live deals keep arriving priced just below it by competitors with different cost structures or no discipline.
poles: hold the documented floor
match the market to win the deal
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the floor holds; the response to a below-floor rival is scope repositioning or a calm walk-away, with exceptions written, dated, and rare

conflict_axes.name: segment_upside_vs_operational_burden
conflict_axes.description: Motels bring the biggest installs with the heaviest compliance and wiring burden; restaurants bring fast vivid sales with mortality-driven write-offs; offices bring quiet durable seats.
poles: chase large vivid deals
compound quiet durable seats
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: weight the scorecard on lifetime economics per support hour, not on install-day revenue, and let the ranking decide

conflict_axes.name: regulatory_simplicity_vs_margin_capture
conflict_axes.description: Agency leaves USF-class and tax obligations with the carrier at the cost of margin; resale captures margin at the cost of possible provider-of-record duties.
poles: stay regulatorily simple as an agent
capture margin and carry the compliance posture
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never trade up the margin ladder ahead of professional verification; the assessment cost is part of the model's price

conflict_axes.name: bundled_goodwill_vs_billable_boundaries
conflict_axes.description: Generous included support builds the goodwill that retains small-town customers; strict billable boundaries protect the seat economics the book is priced on.
poles: include generously and eat the minutes
bill precisely at the written boundary
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: write the boundary honestly, price the included allowance into the seat, and spend deliberate goodwill exceptions where retention value is real

conflict_axes.name: close_speed_vs_buyer_protection
conflict_axes.description: Month-end pressure and easy buyers pull toward fast closes; the vulnerable-buyer and disclosure disciplines deliberately slow exactly those deals.
poles: close while the buyer is warm
slow down and protect the buyer's understanding
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: buyer protection dominates: plain-language written disclosure and time to decide, accepting the losses that discipline costs

edge_cases.description: A prospect under a white-label pitch asks directly whether the operator is the actual carrier
edge_cases.mitigation: answer truthfully with the prepared disclosure script: the brand, support, and accountability are the operator's, the platform and carriage are named partners in the contract

edge_cases.description: A motel owner wants the cheapest possible quote and pushes to drop the E911 room-level scoping
edge_cases.trigger: price negotiation attacks the compliance line on a room-phone deal
edge_cases.mitigation: offer cost cuts anywhere else (phone models, phased rooms, training hours) and hold the E911 scoping as non-removable; decline the deal if the owner insists

edge_cases.description: A restaurant customer folds mid-term owing service fees with rented hardware on site
edge_cases.trigger: business failure in the high-mortality segment
edge_cases.mitigation: deal shape planned for this: deposit-class protections, hardware recovery terms, and write-off exposure priced into segment economics rather than discovered

edge_cases.description: A prospect demands a written guarantee of total uptime before signing
edge_cases.trigger: guarantee language is made a closing condition
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse absolute guarantee words; offer the upstream provider's published SLA passed through honestly plus the operator's written response commitments, and let the deal go if that is insufficient

edge_cases.description: A dental office manager asks whether the phone system is HIPAA compliant before the demo continues
edge_cases.trigger: a compliance-adjacent question the operator cannot lawfully self-certify
edge_cases.mitigation: state what the system demonstrably does, route the compliance determination to the platform vendor's terms and a qualified advisor, and never assert the compliance conclusion

edge_cases.description: The upstream carrier unilaterally amends the agent commission schedule for existing referrals
edge_cases.mitigation: re-read the amended clauses against the mechanics checklist (evergreen, clawback, assignability), rescore the model decision, and accelerate diversification if the residual base is impaired

edge_cases.description: A competitor quotes a seat price below the operator's computed wholesale-plus-support floor
edge_cases.trigger: a below-floor quote surfaces in a live deal
edge_cases.mitigation: hold the floor, decompose scope differences for the buyer (what the low quote omits: install, support boundary, E911 scoping), and walk calmly if price is the only axis

edge_cases.description: A trucking prospect wants almost no desk phones, only driver softphones on personal devices
edge_cases.trigger: the seat mix collapses toward mobile-only extensions
edge_cases.mitigation: use the softphone-heavy option pack with honest expectations about personal-device support boundaries written into the support scope

edge_cases.description: A prospect switching from a rival's white-label service cannot say who controls their numbers
edge_cases.trigger: number ownership is unclear at the sales stage of a switch deal
edge_cases.mitigation: record the ownership question as unanswered, obtain account and porting-authority facts before promising any cutover date, and pass the verified answer to the deployment discipline
