edge_cases.description: An elderly motel owner with limited English agrees to everything in the first meeting
edge_cases.trigger: a vulnerable buyer shows no resistance to a substantial commitment
edge_cases.mitigation: slow the close deliberately: plain-language written summary of total costs and term, invite a family member or advisor, and give explicit time to decide before signature

edge_cases.description: A multi-site office prospect wants one agreement covering locations with very different needs
edge_cases.trigger: one buyer, several sites, divergent seat shapes
edge_cases.mitigation: one master agreement with per-site option packs and per-site E911 and porting flags, priced from the same core bundle rather than a bespoke build

edge_cases.description: The prospect cannot produce a current phone bill for the savings comparison they asked for
edge_cases.trigger: a savings claim is requested with no auditable baseline
edge_cases.mitigation: make no savings claim; sell features, accountability, and the offer's own price on its merits, and offer to run the bill audit when the documents surface

workflow.action: Frame the business and its revenue stack
workflow.description: State the four revenue layers, the stage boundary, and the two handoff artifacts this stage owes downstream
workflow.gate: all four layers, the stage scope, and both handoff artifacts are stated

workflow.description: Answer who bills, who owns the customer, and who carries the risk for agent, reseller, and white-label
workflow.gate: the three ownership answers are distinct and written for all three models

workflow.action: Detail each model's economics as mechanisms
workflow.description: Write the commission, margin, and dependency mechanics for all three models with every figure deferred to live agreements
workflow.gate: no invented figure appears; each economic quantity names the agreement or rate card that will supply it

workflow.action: Screen regulatory and tax exposure per model
workflow.description: List the USF-class, telecom-tax, registration, and 911-fee obligation classes per candidate model and route them to professional verification
workflow.gate: obligations are named by class with a verify-with-a-qualified-professional flag, and no position is asserted

workflow.description: Score the models on capital, support capacity, compliance appetite, and exit ambition; record the choice, the hybrid rules, and the losers
workflow.gate: all four criteria are scored in writing and the regulatory and E911 flags are carried into the memo

workflow.description: Apply the five screening criteria to dental, trucking, restaurant, motel, and office with observed evidence per criterion
workflow.gate: each profile scores all five criteria with at least one observed example each

workflow.description: Declare weights, score each profiled segment, and pick one or two beachheads with a written parking decision for the rest
workflow.gate: weights were declared before scoring and the beachhead pick names one or two segments only

workflow.description: Assemble the core bundle, its vertical option packs, the purchase-versus-rental fork, and the mandatory E911 line
workflow.gate: every bundle variant carries the E911 scoping line and discloses any amortized structure with term and total

workflow.description: Write included-versus-billable work classes, honest response language, and the escalation handoff for the chosen model
workflow.gate: the scope is written, model-consistent, and signed off as a pricing input

workflow.action: Construct seat prices and the floor
workflow.description: Build each tier's seat price from rate card, support allocation, pass-through treatment, and margin; compute the floor
workflow.gate: every input shows its source and verification date and the floor is computed from the operator's own costs

workflow.action: Draft honest positioning against each rival class
workflow.description: Map copper incumbents, national self-serve brands, and local rivals to truthful counters that pass the substantiation gate
workflow.gate: every positioning sentence maps to its substantiation and no fear-selling device appears

workflow.description: Run the seven-line definition-of-done on every signed deal and bounce failures back to their owning node
workflow.gate: all seven checklist lines are answered, including the recorded number-ownership answer

dominance_rules.rule: The E911 scoping flag dominates every economic consideration on every deal
dominance_rules.rationale: the duty class exists for life safety and a skipped flag poisons the deployment and the operator's standing at once
dominance_rules.trigger: any quote, discount negotiation, or bundle variant that would remove or dilute E911 scoping
dominance_rules.action: hold the scoping line, offer cuts elsewhere, and decline the deal if compliance is the price of winning it

dominance_rules.rule: Claim substantiation dominates positioning appeal: an unverifiable claim is cut, not softened
dominance_rules.rationale: one falsifiable claim discovered by a customer costs more book value than the deals it closed
dominance_rules.trigger: a savings, uptime, or capability claim lacking its bill audit, published SLA, or demo evidence
dominance_rules.action: remove the claim from materials and conversation until its evidence exists

dominance_rules.rule: Professional regulatory verification dominates margin attraction when choosing or changing models
dominance_rules.rationale: provider-of-record obligations discovered after invoicing are retroactive in effect and can dwarf the margin that motivated the move
dominance_rules.trigger: a model change or new jurisdiction is contemplated for margin reasons
dominance_rules.action: obtain the qualified professional assessment before the first invoice under the new posture

dominance_rules.rule: Recurring durability dominates upfront harvest when one-time and monthly pricing conflict
dominance_rules.rationale: the business's asset is the MRR book; one-time revenue exists to protect it, not to compete with it
dominance_rules.trigger: a deal structure that pads one-time revenue at the expense of seat margin or vice versa
dominance_rules.action: price one-time to cover cost, keep margin in the monthly, and disclose any amortization fully

dominance_rules.rule: The documented floor dominates competitive matching
dominance_rules.rationale: a floor broken once becomes a book-wide repricing through referrals and renewals
dominance_rules.trigger: a below-floor competitor quote or a strategic-logo temptation
dominance_rules.action: reposition scope or walk away; any exception is written, dated, justified, and rare

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure dominates brand story wherever white-label creates ambiguity
dominance_rules.rationale: the customer's consent is only real when they know whose service they are on
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer, contract, or marketing decision touching who runs the network
dominance_rules.action: answer truthfully and keep the platform relationship named in the contract

dominance_rules.rule: Support capacity reality dominates model ambition
dominance_rules.rationale: owning the bill means owning the failure call, and a promise without capacity converts customers into detractors
dominance_rules.trigger: the model decision or support scope tempts commitments beyond what the operator can staff
dominance_rules.action: downgrade the model or narrow the written scope until promise and capacity match

dominance_rules.rationale: a commitment a buyer did not understand is a churn event and an ethical failure already in motion
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer shows limited English, limited technical familiarity, advanced age, or visible confusion
dominance_rules.action: slow the process: plain-language written disclosure, total costs stated, an advisor invited, and time to decide given

anti_rework_rules.rule: Answer the triad's three ownership questions in writing before signing any partner or platform agreement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering after launch that the carrier owns the customers the operator thought it was building a book of

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain the professional regulatory assessment before issuing the first invoice under a chosen model
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-papering every customer and unwinding an invoicing posture after obligations surface

anti_rework_rules.rule: Choose the channel model before architecting the bundle or pricing a single seat
anti_rework_rules.prevents: re-quoting the whole pipeline when the model change alters pass-through treatment and support promises

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the support scope before computing seat prices, and recompute the floor whenever scope widens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a book of seats priced for a support promise lighter than the one customers were given

anti_rework_rules.rule: Profile segments from observed evidence before building vertical option packs
anti_rework_rules.prevents: engineering packs for imagined pain and rebuilding them after the first real installs

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the bill audit before any savings statement is drafted for a prospect
anti_rework_rules.prevents: walking back an unsubstantiated savings claim mid-deal or, worse, after signature

anti_rework_rules.rule: Ask and record the number-ownership question before promising any cutover date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: mid-deployment port rejections that unwind schedules, trust, and sometimes the deal

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the white-label disclosure script before the first branded sales call
anti_rework_rules.prevents: improvised answers about who runs the network hardening into claims that must later be corrected

iteration_protocol.trigger: several deals in one segment are lost on price in a quarter
iteration_protocol.action: re-run the scorecard weighting for the segment and re-examine the bundle and floor against the observed competitive set

iteration_protocol.trigger: realized support minutes per seat exceed the allocation the seat price was built on
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the floor with observed minutes and either reprice new deals or narrow the written included scope

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream partner changes wholesale rates, commission schedules, or program terms
iteration_protocol.action: re-read the amended agreement against the mechanics checklists and rescore the model decision memo

iteration_protocol.trigger: a change in the USF-class or E911 rule families is announced
iteration_protocol.action: route the change to professional verification, update the exposure flag list, and re-check quote templates for the scoping line

iteration_protocol.trigger: an unprofiled vertical produces repeated inbound demand
iteration_protocol.action: apply the five screening criteria to the new vertical and add it to the scorecard as a candidate

iteration_protocol.trigger: a positioning counter fails repeatedly in live deals or a claim is challenged
iteration_protocol.action: pull the claim, re-verify its substantiation, and redraft the counter from evidence that holds

iteration_protocol.trigger: handoff packets bounce repeatedly on the same checklist line
iteration_protocol.action: trace the failing line to its owning node, repair that node's artifact or practice, and only then resume gating

priority_rationale: The frame and the channel triad come first because every downstream artifact - mechanics, exposure flags, the model decision - is shaped by who bills, who owns the customer, and who carries the risk; the compliance flags (regulatory exposure, E911) are set before the model is chosen so the choice inherits them rather than discovering them; segment profiling and the scorecard precede offer work so the bundle is built for validated beachheads; the support scope precedes seat pricing because the promise is a cost input; positioning follows pricing and the claims gate so every counter is substantiated and floor-backed; and the handoff gate comes last because it composes all prior artifacts into the definition-of-done that deployment inherits.
